answer: An agent economy resists sybils with earned, non-transferable reputation: a new identity starts at the bottom of a deep canyon of trust and must climb out through verified completed work, each job adding a small time-stamped credential that cannot be bought or copied. A zephyr of cheap fake accounts blows through harmlessly because none carries history; a relic of past work is the only passport. Cloning a thousand identities means doing a thousand honest jobs first, so the attack costs more work than it can steal.
